data.name: Naomia
data.long_meaning: The name Naomia is derived from the Hebrew word ‘Naham’, which means ‘Comfort’ or ‘Console’. In the Bible, the character Naomi is a woman who loses her husband and her two sons. She returns from Moab to Bethlehem, only to discover that her husband’s kinsman, Boaz, has married her daughter-in-law, Ruth. Despite this, Naomi is comforted when Ruth gives birth to a son, Obed, who becomes the grandfather of King David and an ancestor of Jesus.

in_hebrew.name: נעומיה
in_hebrew.meaning: נעומיה היא שם שפירושו ' נעימה' או 'מתוקה' בעברית
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נעומיה הוא שם עברי שמקורו בשם נעמה, שפירושו 'נעימה' או 'מתוקה'. השם נעמי מוזכר בספר רות, ומשמעותו קשורה לנעימות ולמתיקות. השם נעומיה הוא גרסה נשית של השם נעמי, ומשמעותו היא 'אלה שמביאות נעימות' או 'נעימות אלוהים'.

in_greek.name: Ναομία
in_greek.meaning: Ναομία σημαίνει 'η χαρά' ή 'η ευχαριστία' στην ελληνική
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ναομία είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος נעמי (Naomi), που σημαίνει 'η χαρά' ή 'η ευχαριστία'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα Naomi αναφέρεται στη μητέρα της Ρουθ, και η σημασία του συνδέεται με την χαρά και την ευχαριστία. Το όνομα Ναομία είναι δημοφιλές στην παράδοση των Χριστιανικών ονομάτων.

in_latin.name: Naomia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Naomia est forma Latina nomine hebraeo נעמי (Naomi), quod significat 'gratia' vel 'suavis'. In Ecclesia primitiva Christiana, nomen Naomi referebatur ad matrem Ruth, et significatio eius coniungitur cum gratia et suavitate. Nomen Naomia est usitatum in traditione nominum Christianorum.

The name Naomia carries a rich spiritual significance, embodying qualities of kindness, warmth, and joy. It is a popular Christian name reflecting virtues of pleasantness and loveliness.

data.cultural_impact: The name Naomia carries a powerful message of perseverance, strength, and consolation through difficult times. In Jewish and Christian cultures, Naomi is celebrated for her resilience and determination in the face of loss. Her story is often used to illustrate the importance of family, faith, and community in times of hardship.

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament, Naomi is a Moabite woman who loses her husband and both her sons in a famine. She returns to her hometown in Israel with her daughter-in-law Ruth, who later marries Boaz and becomes the great-grandmother of King David.

St. Naomia of Rome is a 5th century Roman martyr. According to legend, she was a virgin who was arrested for her faith and sent to a brothel under the command of the prefect Almachius. She refused to comply and was executed.
